# Indikator 8

Indikator 8 is a quality indicator from the Danish ADHD database (ADHD-databasen), used to track how well the healthcare system delivers structured education about ADHD to adult patients. Specifically, it measures the share of treatment courses (behandlingsforløb) among adults with an ADHD diagnosis in which the patient began ADHD-related psychoeducation no later than 120 days after the start of treatment [^src1].

The indicator appears in the ADHD database's annual report covering the period 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025 [^src1]. For this reporting period, national compliance with Indikator 8 was measured at 36 percent, with a confidence interval of 34–38 percent [^src1]. This is a low result relative to the report's stated development target of ≥90 percent, a shortfall that runs across most of the indicator set in this report. Indikator 8 belongs to a cluster of four new indicators — Indikator 8 through Indikator 11 — that relate specifically to adults with an ADHD diagnosis; because this patient group and its indicators are being reported for the first time, the results are presented without historical comparison [^src1].

At the regional level, Region Hovedstaden reported a psychoeducation compliance rate of 32 percent for Indikator 8, which the region itself characterizes as far below the development target, though only marginally under the national average for psychoeducation [^src2]. This places [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]]'s performance close to, but slightly below, the nationwide figure of 36 percent [^src1] [^src2].

Indikator 8 sits within the broader context of the ADHD database's ongoing effort to revise its indicator set so that it better reflects clinical practice in ADHD assessment and treatment across Denmark. The annual report documents both the national results for all 11 quality indicators and regional commentary from Denmark's five regions, several of which flagged registration problems and implementation challenges affecting indicator performance more broadly.
